talks.title: US Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board
talks.teaser: PCLOB Board Member Travis LeBlanc analyzes government surveillance authorities, constitutional protections, and civil liberties oversight.
talks.summary:
Travis LeBlanc, board member of the United States Privacy and Civil Liberties Oversight Board (PCLOB), delivers a keynote on federal surveillance oversight and civil liberties protections in the Ethics Village [00:00].

LeBlanc reviews the statutory mandate of PCLOB in monitoring executive branch counterterrorism programs, highlighting the board's deep-dive oversight review of the National Security Agency's (NSA) Section 215 call detail record (CDR) bulk metadata collection program [09:35]. He addresses emerging ethical challenges at the intersection of privacy and technology, examining racial bias in commercial facial recognition algorithms deployed by federal agencies [19:30], emergency data tracking during public health crises [29:15], and whether Congress should expand PCLOB's jurisdiction beyond counterterrorism to broader surveillance and commercial data surveillance [38:35, 49:05].
